title: SLO slip during deployment migration: cascade analysis and guardrail roadmap
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-27 a staged control-plane migration intended to rebalance model routing across regions coincided with a spike of short-lived high-concurrency requests from two customers. The result was a cascading degradation: KV cache cold-misses, aggressive autoscaler scale-downs in the primary region, and prolonged circuit-breaker hysteresis that routed excess traffic into the secondary region and triggered load-shedding. This ticket contains the incident analysis, immediate mitigations, and a prioritized guardrail roadmap to prevent recurrence.
timeline:
2026-02-27T09:05Z - 09:12Z: Deployment migration begins (control-plane config roll, region preference shifts)
2026-02-27T09:13Z - 09:20Z: Two high-concurrency customers issue large prefix-heavy workloads (sustained burst for ~7 minutes)
2026-02-27T09:18Z: Primary region experienced rapid KV cache miss rate increase (cache hit ratio dropped from 94% to 12%)
2026-02-27T09:20Z - 09:27Z: Autoscaler interpreted worker CPU bursts as short spikes and executed rapid scale-downs during perceived cooldown windows, reducing worker pool by ~40%
2026-02-27T09:24Z: Circuit breaker hysteresis thresholds prevented immediate trip; routing spilled over to secondary region and triggered regional load-shedding policies
2026-02-27T09:30Z: On-call engaged, temporary manual routing policy applied to limit per-customer concurrency and pin to regional capacity
2026-02-27T09:45Z: KV cache warmup scripts and conservative autoscaler cooldown patch deployed; SLOs returned below breach threshold by 10:00Z
impact: SLOs affected: 95th-tail latency SLO (<=200ms) breached for text-gen in eu-west-1 and us-west-2 for ~35 minutes. Customer-facing: 3 high-volume customers experienced >30% request errors or rate-limited responses during the peak window. Internal: alert fatigue due to multiple overlapping alarms, increased egress costs from cross-region failover, and one on-call escalation to PageOps.
root_cause: Confluence of factors: (1) control-plane routing migration changed per-customer regional affinity without coordinated cache pre-warm or staged rollout for high-prefix workloads; (2) autoscaler cooldown and metric windowing were tuned for steady-state CPU, not prefix-heavy spikes, causing premature scale-downs; (3) circuit-breaker hysteresis used long open/half-open durations that delayed protective routing, causing overflow into secondary regions; (4) lack of a per-customer concurrency cap and no fast-path for cache-warmup when affinity changes occurred.
mitigation: Immediate mitigations applied during incident: temporarily pinned high-volume customers to origin region, throttled per-customer concurrency at the edge, deployed a KV cache pre-warm job that replayed hot prefixes, and adjusted autoscaler cooldown from 5m -> 90s. After stabilization we rolled back the migration for impacted traffic lanes and adjusted circuit-breaker hysteresis values.
